top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) has the cleanest scientific case on the slate: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the light shift while many neutral atoms are interrogated in parallel, a different route to accuracy and stability from single-ion or comb-based work. It is mature, independently reproduced and surpassed, demonstrated at about 1e-18, and the two-name allocation needs no arbitrary exclusion. The citation must stay specific to magic-wavelength lattice trapping to avoid a repeat of the 2005 and 2012 prizes. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is conceptually strong but forces an exclusion (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Hasan) and overlaps somewhat with 2016. P003 (twisted bilayer graphene) is still too early, with the pairing mechanism unsettled. No award ranks last since P001 is a defensible prize.
recusal_note: I direct WACQT at Chalmers, built on superconducting circuits and circuit QED, with colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson in the same area; this would require recusal on any configuration containing B013, but none of the proposals P001, P002 or P003 contains it. No documented connection to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer.
